value: spontaneous alignment of the body along the North-South axis
method: overhead photographs of fish in circular outdoor sales tubs; body axes traced on a 36-segment rosette, converted to magnetic bearings, coded blind to tub orientation; bimodal circular statistics on per-tub mean vectors
conditions: 14,537 fish bearings from photographs of 80 tubs at 25 localities in the Czech Republic, 18 to 24 December 2011, locations revisited about five times (817 sampling sessions) so the same fish may be counted more than once; main result is bimodal for 69 tubs without water inflow: mean axis 8/188 deg, r = 0.437, p = 1.85e-6; unimodal (p = 0.93) and quadrimodal (p = 0.10) tests not significant; tubs with inlet flow switched on were excluded because inflow direction was biased to the south and weakly correlated with bearings (r = 0.045, p < 0.05); no correlation with light direction; electromagnetic pollution was not measured (static field only); a field correlation, not a controlled field manipulation, so the magnetic cause is inferred
